extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers submitting to The Paris Review (literary authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and editorial standards for submitting literary fiction (short stories and short novellas) to The Paris Review, including technical submission specs and the magazine's qualitative expectations of voice, craft, and ambition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Up to 40 pages of prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should be no longer than 40 pages of prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the maximum length allowed; works of ~30–40 pages (short novellas) are acceptable and should still deliver compression and depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: One piece per submission window
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one piece may be submitted per submission window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters should limit each submission opportunity to a single work to respect editorial bandwidth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission windows: Submittable in February, June, October; mail year-round
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic submissions accepted during specified months (February, June, October); mailed submissions may be sent year-round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the stated submission routes and timing; use Submittable during open windows or mail manuscripts at other times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations welcome (with original)
rubrics_metrics.description: Translated works are accepted, but the original-language text must be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include both the translation and the original text when submitting translated work so editors can assess fidelity and craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous submissions OK (notify if accepted elsewhere)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Paris Review permits simultaneous submissions, provided the author notifies the editors if the piece is accepted elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your work is accepted by another outlet while under consideration, you must inform The Paris Review promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary fiction primarily — character-driven, language-driven
rubrics_metrics.description: The magazine primarily publishes literary fiction that is driven by character development and attention to language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference is for works where character and linguistic craft are central rather than plot-oriented genre pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wide stylistic latitude — from realism to experimental, with high craft demanded throughout
rubrics_metrics.description: The Paris Review accepts a broad range of styles (realism to experimental) but expects high craft in any chosen mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stylistic variety is allowed, but every submission must demonstrate consistently strong technique and control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive voice — recognized within first paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: A distinctive authorial voice should be evident quickly — ideally within the first paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voice that immediately marks the work as singular helps capture editorial attention; weak or generic openings are discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural / intellectual ambition — engagement with ideas, history, art, philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should demonstrate cultural or intellectual ambition, engaging with ideas, history, art, or philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magazine values fiction that converses with larger intellectual concerns rather than purely surface-level entertainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence-level mastery — every line should reward attention
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must show mastery at the sentence level; each line should be crafted to reward close reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Close attention to diction, rhythm, and sentence construction is expected; stray or careless lines undermine the whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compression and depth — even 30–40 page novellas hit hard
rubrics_metrics.description: Even relatively short works (30–40 pages) are expected to achieve both compression and emotional/intellectual depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economy of material combined with layered meaning is preferred over padding or superficial length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resonance over plot mechanics — the lingering effect after reading
rubrics_metrics.description: The lasting resonance or after-effect of a story is valued more highly than mechanical plotting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should aim to leave readers with emotional or intellectual reverberation rather than merely executing plot turns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor recommendation: Read the most recent issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective submitters are advised to read recent issues to familiarize themselves with the magazine's published material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewing recent content helps align submissions with the magazine's tastes and standards; it's an explicit editorial suggestion for applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: publish the best new writing
rubrics_metrics.description: The magazine's foundational mission is to publish the best new writing, setting a high-quality bar for submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should aim for excellence consistent with the magazine's historic standards and editorial ambitions.
